statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 8 with NQ observed at 29,596.25, up 0.19% from the 29,538.75 settle and still inside the two-sided 29,489.75-29,625.50 Globex band, roughly 29 points below a range high it has not extended. An overnight Iranian missile launch at U.S. targets in Jordan was intercepted and left NQ, ES and VIX futures broadly unchanged, so escalation is not being transmitted into price path. Stress holds at 75 with Brent at $98.95 on a sixth straight advance and the 10-year at 4.796%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-15:00 UTC, the U.S. cash open and first full hour, where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the most plausible route to repeated extension after failed retracements. A secondary checkpoint cluster sits at 17:00 UTC, combining the 10-year note auction with the Apple keynote, and a third at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: NQ holds the 29,489.75-29,625.50 Globex band at 29,596.25 with tail at 8, while Brent $98.95 and a 4.796% 10-year keep stress at 75
body: At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 shows no evidence of mean-reversion failure. NQ futures trade at 29,596.25, up 57.50 points or 0.19% from the 29,538.75 settle, inside a Globex range of 29,489.75-29,625.50. That band is 135.75 points, about 0.46% wide, two-sided, and it has not been extended during the current hour despite price sitting close to its upper edge. Investing.com corroborates the level at 29,595.25 and the same 0.19% change. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,686.25 are up 0.07% in a 17-point range, so cross-index behaviour is contained rather than directional. The cash Nasdaq-100 closed the prior session at 29,507.70, down 0.12%, after a two-sided 29,400.70-29,655.73 range, and it closed near the middle of that range rather than at an extreme. The macro backdrop is the source of stress, not the tape. Brent is at $98.95, up 1.05% on a sixth consecutive advance, with WTI at $93.88, both pressing toward levels last seen three months ago on Gulf supply disruption. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.796%, close to its highest since 2023, and the 2-year stands at 4.37% on the latest H.15 release. Futures markets price roughly a 60% probability of a 25 basis-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC after August payrolls printed 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus. Despite that combination, VIX closed at 15.72, which is a notable conflict between realised equity volatility and the rates and energy channels. Overnight the U.S.-Iran tanker conflict escalated again: Iran launched ballistic missiles toward U.S. targets in Jordan, of which 18 were intercepted with no reported casualties, and Iranian officials described plans for a maritime exclusion zone in the Strait of Hormuz where transit would require permission. Reported Hormuz traffic has fallen to roughly ten vessels per day, the lowest since May. That escalation is a genuine unresolved discontinuity mechanism and it is why tail sits at 8 rather than at the floor, but it has so far produced no gap, no one-way extension and no failed-retracement structure in index futures. Internal index composition also argues for rotation rather than trend: on 8 September six of eight megacaps closed lower, led by NVIDIA at -2.01%, while semiconductors were strongly bid with Intel +9.05%, Advanced Micro Devices +5.90%, ARM +3.74% and Qualcomm +3.17%. Dominant mode is therefore mixed. The session ahead contains no Tier-1 U.S. release; the flagged window is the 13:30-15:00 UTC cash open and first full hour, with a secondary cluster at 17:00 UTC where a 10-year note auction into a multi-year-high yield coincides with Apple's product keynote. Producer prices and jobless claims follow on 10 September and August CPI on 11 September, both outside this forecast window.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours the mapped state stayed EA_ON throughout, with tail between 5 and 15 and no reading approaching the block threshold. The single elevated print was 15 at 14:00 UTC on 8 September during a brief trend-down phase in the first full U.S. cash hour, and it reverted within that same hour. One hour, 09:00 UTC on 8 September, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Stress rose steadily from 64 to a 75 peak as crude pressed toward $100 on Gulf supply disruption and the 10-year held near multi-year highs, while confidence improved from 84 to 89 as live price-path evidence accumulated. Dominant mode was mixed for 22 of the 23 available hours, with one trend-down and one normal reading, which is consistent with an index rotating inside a range rather than trending.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain no Tier-1 U.S. macro release; PPI and jobless claims on 10 September at 12:30 UTC fall just outside the window. Conditional tail stays in an 8-13 band and never approaches the block threshold, peaking at 13 across the 13:30-15:00 UTC U.S. cash open where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the specific failure mode of concern. Secondary steps sit at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.796% yield coincides with the Apple keynote, and at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Stress holds in a 74-77 band because it is carried by Brent near $99, a 10-year close to multi-year highs and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz escalation rather than by observed price structure. Confidence decays from 88 to 79 with distance from live evidence rather than because the view changes.
